name: @pyworkload/3x-ui-mcp

tools.name: add_client
tools.description: Add a new client (user) and attach it to one or more inbounds. Clients are first-class, email-keyed entities. A UUID is auto-generated for VMess/VLESS if not provided; for Trojan/Shadowsocks/Hysteria the panel generates the key server-side when omitted. Field meanings and units: read the xui://docs/client-fields resource.

ad_tag.description: MTProto advertising tag from @MTProxybot: exactly 32 hex characters, or the panel rejects it

expiry_time.description: Expiry as Unix timestamp in milliseconds (0 = never)

inbound_ids.description: IDs of the inbounds to attach this client to (at least one)

keep_alive.description: WireGuard PersistentKeepalive in seconds; 0 sends none. Omit to keep the stored value

limit_hwid.description: Max devices (HWIDs) that may register for this client, 0 = unlimited. See list_client_devices

reset.description: Traffic auto-reset period in days (0 = off)

reset_day.description: Calendar day of the month the traffic quota renews, 1-31. 0 keeps the interval mode set by 'reset'

reset_max.description: How many times the quota may auto-renew, 0 = unlimited

reset_weekday.description: Weekday the quota renews, 1-7 (Mon-Sun); 0 disables weekly renewal. Cannot be combined with 'reset' or 'reset_day' — update_client zeroes those when switching to weekly. Panel v3.9.0+

reverse_tag.description: VLESS simple reverse proxy tag. Pass an empty string to clear it

secret.description: MTProto per-client secret, used to build the tg://proxy link

sub_id.description: Subscription ID for subscription links (auto-generated if empty)

traffic_reset.description: Per-client traffic reset cycle, independent of the inbound's own

traffic_reset_day.description: Day of the cycle the per-client reset fires, 1-31

uuid.description: Client UUID (for VMess/VLESS). Auto-generated if empty

tools.name: add_clients_to_group
tools.description: Label many clients with one group in a single call. A client belongs to at most one group, so this replaces any group it was in.

emails.description: Emails of the clients to add

tools.name: add_host_group
tools.description: Create a host group. inbound_ids and remark are required unless raw_json carries them.

is_disabled.description: Disable the group without deleting it

is_hidden.description: Keep the group out of subscription output

port.description: Port to advertise; 0 keeps the inbound's own port

raw_json.description: Complete HostGroup JSON. When given it is sent as-is and every other parameter is ignored — use it for fields this tool does not expose.

security.description: TLS mode to advertise; 'same' inherits the inbound's

server_description.description: Note shown next to the group (max 64 chars)

tags.description: Free-form tags used to filter host groups

tools.name: add_node
tools.description: Register a node. The panel probes it before saving, so unreachable details are rejected rather than stored. api_token is required unless the node is set up for mTLS.

allow_private_address.description: Permit a private or loopback address, which the panel otherwise rejects

api_token.description: The node's API token. Write-only: the panel never returns it, and omitting it on an update keeps the stored one.

base_path.description: Node panel base path, e.g. / or /xui/

clear_api_token.description: Drop the stored API token — for a node switched to mTLS. Cannot be combined with api_token.

enable.description: Whether traffic sync with this node runs

inbound_sync_mode.description: Push every inbound to the node, or only the tagged ones

inbound_tags.description: Inbound tags to sync when inbound_sync_mode=selected

name.description: Node name, unique in this panel

outbound_tag.description: Reach the node through this Xray outbound instead of directly

pinned_cert_sha256.description: Base64 SHA-256 of the node's leaf certificate, for tls_verify_mode=pin

scheme.description: How to reach the node panel

tls_verify_mode.description: How the node's certificate is checked: verify (normal), skip, pin (see get_node_cert_fingerprint), or mtls

tools.name: add_routing_rule
tools.description:
Add a new routing rule to the Xray config. The rule is a JSON object. Common fields:
- "type": "field" (always)
- "outboundTag": target outbound name (e.g. "direct", "blocked", "proxy")
- "domain": array of domain patterns (e.g. ["geosite:google", "domain:example.com"])
- "ip": array of IP patterns (e.g. ["geoip:private", "geoip:ru"])
- "port": port or range (e.g. "80,443", "1000-2000")
- "protocol": array of protocols (e.g. ["bittorrent"])
- "inboundTag": array of inbound tags to match
- "network": "tcp", "udp", or "tcp,udp"

Example: {"type":"field","outboundTag":"direct","domain":["geosite:category-ru"]}

index.description: Position to insert at (0-based). If omitted, appends to end. Rules are evaluated in order — earlier rules take priority.

tools.name: attach_client
tools.description: Attach an existing client to additional inbounds, by email.

inbound_ids.description: Inbound IDs to attach the client to

tools.name: backup_to_telegram
tools.description: Send a fresh database backup to every Telegram chat configured as an admin recipient. The backup contains every client credential, so it goes wherever those chats are.

tools.name: bulk_adjust_clients
tools.description: Shift expiry and traffic quota for many clients in one call — the bulk renewal. Both deltas may be negative. Clients on unlimited expiry or unlimited traffic are reported as skipped instead of being given a limit.

add_days.description: Days to add to each expiry date; negative shortens it

add_gb.description: GB to add to each traffic quota; negative reduces it

emails.description: Emails of the clients to adjust

flow.description: Set this flow on every listed client (e.g. 'xtls-rprx-vision'). Omit to leave each client's flow alone.

tools.name: bulk_attach_clients
tools.description: Attach many existing clients to many inbounds in one call. Each client keeps its email, UUID, subId and its shared traffic row, so the same credentials work on every inbound it is attached to.

emails.description: Emails of the clients to attach

tools.name: bulk_create_clients
tools.description: Create many clients at once across the same set of inbounds, sharing common limits. Each client gets an auto-generated UUID.

emails.description: Emails of the clients to create

expiry_time.description: Shared expiry as Unix ms (0 = never)

inbound_ids.description: Inbound IDs to attach every created client to

total_gb.description: Shared traffic limit in GB (0 = unlimited)

tools.name: bulk_delete_clients
tools.description: Delete many clients at once by email.

emails.description: Emails of the clients to delete

tools.name: bulk_delete_host_groups
tools.description: Delete several host groups in one call.

tools.name: bulk_delete_inbounds
tools.description: Delete several inbounds in one call. The panel processes them sequentially, reports failures per id while the rest still proceed, and restarts Xray at most once. Cannot be undone.

ids.description: Inbound IDs as a JSON array, e.g. [3,7,12]

tools.name: bulk_detach_clients
tools.description: Detach many clients from many inbounds without deleting them. A client detached from its last inbound keeps existing but is served nowhere — delete_orphan_clients is what removes those.

emails.description: Emails of the clients to detach

tools.name: bulk_disable_clients
tools.description: Disable many clients at once, one rewrite per owning inbound. Their configuration is kept, so bulk_enable_clients reverses it.

emails.description: Emails of the clients to disable

tools.name: bulk_enable_clients
tools.description: Enable many clients at once. Emails are grouped by inbound, so each inbound is rewritten once. Clients that do not exist come back in a 'skipped' list rather than failing the call.

emails.description: Emails of the clients to enable

tools.name: bulk_reset_traffic
tools.description: Reset traffic counters for a specific set of clients, by email.

emails.description: Emails of the clients whose traffic to reset

tools.name: bulk_set_host_groups_enable
tools.description: Enable or disable several host groups at once.

enable.description: true to enable, false to disable

tools.name: clear_client_devices
tools.description: Drop every registered device for a client so new ones can register — the fix for a user who changed phones and hit the HWID limit.

tools.name: clear_client_ips
tools.description: Clear all recorded IP addresses for a client.

tools.name: create_api_token
tools.description: Mint a scoped API token. The plaintext is in the response and nowhere else — the panel keeps a SHA-256 hash — so it has to be captured now or the token is unusable. Scope 'admin' grants the whole API (what this MCP server needs), 'monitor' only the status and metrics routes, 'node-sync' only the panel-to-node allowlist.

expires_at.description: Expiry as Unix milliseconds; 0 never expires

tools.name: create_client_group
tools.description: Create an empty client group. It becomes selectable in client forms before it has any members. Fails if the name is taken.

tools.name: create_inbound
tools.description: Create a new inbound connection. The 'settings', 'stream_settings' and 'sniffing' parameters are JSON strings in 3x-ui format; read the xui://docs/inbound-settings resource for a worked example per protocol and transport.

expiry_time.description: Expiry time as Unix timestamp in milliseconds (0 = never)

protocol.description: Protocol: vmess, vless, trojan, shadowsocks, dokodemo-door, socks, http

settings.description: Protocol-specific settings as JSON string (includes clients array)

stream_settings.description: Transport/stream settings as JSON string. Default: TCP with no TLS

total.description: Total traffic limit in bytes (0 = unlimited)

tools.name: create_outbound_sub
tools.description: Add an outbound subscription. The panel fetches the URL, parses it into outbounds with stable tags derived from tag_prefix, and merges them into the config additively — the template's own outbounds stay.

allow_insecure.description: Accept TLS outbounds with certificate verification disabled

allow_private.description: Accept outbounds pointing at private/LAN addresses

prepend.description: Place these outbounds before the template's own — the first outbound is Xray's default route

tag_prefix.description: Prefix for the generated outbound tags, e.g. 'sub1-'

tools.name: create_sub_balancer
tools.description: Create a subscription balancer over a set of inbounds.

enabled.description: Whether the balancer is served to clients

sort_order.description: Position in the balancer list; 1 sorts first

strategy.description: How the client app picks a server

tools.name: delete_all_inbound_clients
tools.description: Remove every client attached to one inbound, keeping the inbound itself. Clients attached to other inbounds as well are deleted panel-wide, since clients are email-keyed entities. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: delete_api_token
tools.description: Permanently delete an API token. Anything authenticating with it stops working immediately and the token cannot be recovered — set_api_token_enabled is the reversible option.

scope.description: The token's stored scope; the panel refuses the delete unless it matches

tools.name: delete_client
tools.description: Remove a client (from all its inbounds) by email.

keep_traffic.description: Preserve the client's traffic statistics after deletion

tools.name: delete_client_device
tools.description: Remove one registered device from a client, freeing a single slot under its HWID limit.

tools.name: delete_client_group
tools.description: Delete a client group and clear the label from its members. The clients themselves are kept — use bulk_delete_clients to remove them.

tools.name: delete_depleted_clients
tools.description: Remove all clients panel-wide that have exhausted their traffic or expired.

tools.name: delete_host_group
tools.description: Delete a host group and every host inside it. The inbounds it published are untouched.

tools.name: delete_inbound
tools.description: Permanently delete an inbound and all its associated client data. This action cannot be undone.

tools.name: delete_node
tools.description: Delete a node. Inbounds bound to it are not migrated anywhere, so they stop being served until they are reassigned.

tools.name: delete_orphan_clients
tools.description: Delete every client attached to no inbound, together with its traffic record, IP log, devices and external links. Cleans up after inbounds were removed without their clients.

tools.name: delete_outbound_sub
tools.description: Delete an outbound subscription. Its outbounds disappear from the merged config on the next Xray reload; routing rules that referenced their tags will stop matching.

tools.name: delete_sub_balancer
tools.description: Delete a subscription balancer. Clients stop seeing it on their next subscription fetch; the inbounds behind it are untouched.

tools.name: detach_client
tools.description: Detach a client from the given inbounds, by email. The client itself is kept (use delete_client to remove it entirely).

inbound_ids.description: Inbound IDs to detach the client from

tools.name: export_clients
tools.description: Count the clients in the panel and link to the full export at xui://clients/export. The export is the {client, inboundIds} array import_clients takes, so it round-trips — but it carries every UUID and password, so it stays behind the link unless full=true is passed.

full.description: Return the whole export inline instead of a count and a link

tools.name: generate_ech_cert
tools.description: Generate an ECH (Encrypted Client Hello) keypair and config list for one SNI. Nothing is stored — the result goes into an inbound's stream settings.

sni.description: Server name the ECH config is issued for

tools.name: generate_key
tools.description:
Generate key material with the panel's own generators — use this instead of inventing values when building an inbound. Types:
- 'uuid': a UUID v4 for a client id
- 'x25519': X25519 keypair for Reality (privateKey goes into the inbound, publicKey into client links)
- 'vless_enc': VLESS encryption auth options; each entry pairs a decryption string for the inbound with the encryption string for clients
- 'mlkem768': ML-KEM-768 keypair (post-quantum KEM)
- 'mldsa65': ML-DSA-65 keypair (post-quantum signature)

tools.name: get_active_inbounds
tools.description: List the inbound tags that carried traffic in the last heartbeat window, grouped by the node hosting them. Pairs with get_online_clients_by_node to see which node is actually serving what.

tools.name: get_all_inbound_links
tools.description: Count the connection URLs (vless://, vmess://, trojan://, ss://, ...) for every client across every inbound and link to the full list at xui://inbounds/links. The URLs carry client credentials, so they stay behind the link unless full=true is passed.

full.description: Return every connection URL inline instead of a count and a link

tools.name: get_amneziawg_logs
tools.description: Return live AmneziaWG peer activity — last handshake, endpoint, transfer per peer — plus the panel's own AmneziaWG event lines.

count.description: Maximum peer rows and event lines to return

tools.name: get_balancers
tools.description: List the load balancers defined in routing.balancers together with their live state in the running Xray core. For each balancer: the saved definition (selector, fallbackTag, strategy) plus 'live' with running, override (the outbound it is pinned to, if any) and selected (what the strategy picks right now). Routing rules reference a balancer through 'balancerTag' instead of 'outboundTag'.

tools.name: get_cert_hash
tools.description: Compute the SHA-256 of a certificate for pinning (the pinned_peer_cert_sha256 an inbound or host group takes). Pass a path on the panel host, or the certificate inline.

cert_content.description: Certificate content in PEM or DER, as an alternative to cert_file

cert_file.description: Path to a certificate file on the panel host

tools.name: get_client
tools.description: Get a single client's full configuration (UUID, limits, settings) and the inbounds it is attached to, by email.

tools.name: get_client_group_emails
tools.description: List the emails of the clients in one group — the input for fanning a bulk operation across the whole group.

tools.name: get_client_ips
tools.description: Get IP addresses recorded for a client, with timestamps.

tools.name: get_client_ips_by_node
tools.description: List per-client source IPs grouped by the node that observed them — the cluster-wide view behind per-client IP limits.

tools.name: get_client_ips_table
tools.description: Return the aggregated client-IP table — the cluster-wide record of which addresses used which client, and the data per-client IP limits are enforced against.

tools.name: get_client_links
tools.description: Get the connection URLs for one client, one per inbound it is attached to. Keyed by email, so it answers for that client alone — unlike get_subscription_links, which is keyed by subId and returns the links of every client sharing it. Works for a client with no subId.

tools.name: get_client_traffic
tools.description: Get upload/download traffic statistics for a client by email. Returns current usage, limits, and enable status.

tools.name: get_clients_by_telegram_id
tools.description: Look up clients by Telegram user ID. Answers with an array, since several clients can share one Telegram account.

tools.name: get_default_settings
tools.description: Preview the settings a fresh install would compute for this host. Reads only — nothing is applied.

tools.name: get_default_xray_config
tools.description: Get the default Xray configuration template used by the panel.

tools.name: get_factory_defaults
tools.description: Return the shipped default for each setting key, so a stored value can be told apart from the default it would fall back to. Reads only.

tools.name: get_fail2ban_status
tools.description: Report whether per-client IP limits can actually be enforced on this host. Enforcement needs fail2ban installed and usable, so a client's limitIp is inert when this says otherwise.

tools.name: get_happ_link
tools.description: Get an encrypted happ://crypt5 link that wraps a client's subscription URL, for the Happ app. The panel answers only when its happLinkEnable setting is on, subscriptions are enabled and the client has a subId; otherwise it reports 'happ link unavailable' without saying which.

tools.name: get_host_group
tools.description: Get one host group by its group ID (a string, not a number).

tools.name: get_inbound
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific inbound by its ID. Includes protocol settings, stream settings, sniffing config, and per-client stats.

tools.name: get_inbound_fallbacks
tools.description: List the fallback rules on a master VLESS/Trojan TCP-TLS inbound. Each rule routes traffic that matched no client to a child inbound, keyed by SNI, ALPN, path or dest.

tools.name: get_inbound_hosts
tools.description: List the host groups attached to one inbound — what addresses that inbound is currently published under.

tools.name: get_inbound_options
tools.description: Picker projection of the inbounds: id, remark, tag, protocol, port and the server-computed capability flags (such as whether an inbound can carry XTLS flow). Cheaper than list_inbounds when only choosing one.

tools.name: get_last_online
tools.description: Get the last-online timestamp for every client.

tools.name: get_logs
tools.description: Get application logs from the 3x-ui panel.

count.description: Number of log lines to retrieve

level.description: Log level filter: debug, info, warning, error

tools.name: get_metrics_history
tools.description: Time-series for one host metric as {t, v} samples over a window from 2 minutes to 7 days. Use it to see load over time instead of the single instant server_status reports.

bucket.description: Seconds per sample. The panel always returns 60 samples, so this also picks the window: 2 (2m), 30 (30m), 60 (1h), 180 (3h), 360 (6h), 720 (12h), 1440 (24h), 2880 (2d), 10080 (7d).

tools.name: get_node
tools.description: Get one node by ID, including its connection details and sync state. The API token is never returned — only whether one is set.

tools.name: get_node_cert_fingerprint
tools.description: Connect to a node without verifying its certificate and return the leaf's SHA-256 in base64 — the value to pass as pinned_cert_sha256 for a self-signed node.

allow_private_address.description: Permit a private or loopback address, which the panel otherwise rejects

api_token.description: The node's API token. Write-only: the panel never returns it, and omitting it on an update keeps the stored one.

base_path.description: Node panel base path, e.g. / or /xui/

clear_api_token.description: Drop the stored API token — for a node switched to mTLS. Cannot be combined with api_token.

enable.description: Whether traffic sync with this node runs

inbound_sync_mode.description: Push every inbound to the node, or only the tagged ones

inbound_tags.description: Inbound tags to sync when inbound_sync_mode=selected

name.description: Node name, unique in this panel

outbound_tag.description: Reach the node through this Xray outbound instead of directly

pinned_cert_sha256.description: Base64 SHA-256 of the node's leaf certificate, for tls_verify_mode=pin

scheme.description: How to reach the node panel

tls_verify_mode.description: How the node's certificate is checked: verify (normal), skip, pin (see get_node_cert_fingerprint), or mtls

tools.name: get_node_descendants
tools.description: Summarize the nodes below this panel in the cluster tree: guid, parent, name, address, status and versions. This is the view a node reports upward to its parent panel.

tools.name: get_node_history
tools.description: CPU or memory history for one node, in the same {t, v} shape as get_metrics_history.

tools.name: get_node_mtls_ca
tools.description: Return this panel's node-auth CA certificate in PEM, to paste into a node's trust setting. The CA and the master client certificate are minted on the first call, which is why this is not a pure read.

tools.name: get_node_web_cert
tools.description: Ask a node for its own web TLS certificate and key paths, so an inbound assigned to that node points at files that exist there rather than on this panel.

tools.name: get_nordvpn_data
tools.description: Read the NordVPN integration: 'countries' lists available countries, 'servers' lists the servers in one country (pass country_id), 'data' returns the stored account state.

country_id.description: Country ID from action=countries, required for action=servers

tools.name: get_online_clients
tools.description: Get a list of currently connected/active clients.

tools.name: get_online_clients_by_node
tools.description: List online client emails grouped by the node each one is connected to. get_online_clients answers the same question for this panel alone; this one attributes them across the cluster.

tools.name: get_outbounds
tools.description: Get the outbound configurations from the Xray template. Shows all defined outbounds (proxy, direct, blocked, etc.) with their protocols and settings.

tools.name: get_outbounds_traffic
tools.description: Get traffic statistics for all outbound connections.

tools.name: get_panel_update_info
tools.description: Check GitHub for a newer 3x-ui release than the one running.

tools.name: get_panel_update_status
tools.description: Report how the last panel self-update ended: run ID, state and exit code. Compare the run ID against the one update_panel returned to tell a finished run from a stale result.

tools.name: get_pia_data
tools.description: Read the PIA WireGuard integration: 'countries' lists the regions from PIA's signed server list, 'servers' lists the servers in one region (pass country_code), 'data' returns the stored account state.

country_code.description: Region code from action=countries, required for action=servers

tools.name: get_remote_cert_hash
tools.description: Run `xray tls ping` against a remote server and return its live leaf-certificate SHA-256 — the value to pin when you cannot copy the certificate itself.

allow_private.description: Allow a private or loopback target. From panel v3.9.0 such targets are refused without it

tools.name: get_routing_rules
tools.description: Get only the routing section from the Xray template config. Returns the routing object with domainStrategy and rules array.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: Get all 3x-ui panel settings: web server config, Telegram bot, subscription, security, and more.

tools.name: get_subscription_links
tools.description: Get the connection URLs served under a subscription ID — every enabled client whose subId matches, one URL per inbound (and per external proxy where configured). Same set as the public /sub/<subId> endpoint, but as a JSON array instead of base64. A client's subId comes from get_client or list_clients.

tools.name: get_warp_data
tools.description: Read the Cloudflare Warp integration: 'data' returns the account and its quota, 'config' returns the WireGuard configuration the panel holds.

tools.name: get_web_cert_files
tools.description: Return this panel's own web TLS certificate and key file paths.

tools.name: get_xray_config
tools.description: Summarize the Xray configuration the core is running: how many inbounds, outbounds, routing rules and DNS servers it has, plus a link to the full JSON at xui://xray/config. Pass full=true to get the whole document inline instead.

full.description: Return the entire configuration inline instead of a summary and a link

tools.name: get_xray_logs
tools.description: Get Xray proxy access/error logs with optional filtering.

count.description: Number of log lines to retrieve

filter.description: Text filter to search within logs

tools.name: get_xray_metrics
tools.description: Xray runtime metrics state: whether the Xray config has a metrics block, which expvar keys are flowing, and their current values. Returns an empty state when metrics are not configured.

tools.name: get_xray_metrics_history
tools.description: Time-series for one Xray runtime metric (memory, GC and heap counters) over a window from 2 minutes to 7 days.

tools.name: get_xray_observatory
tools.description: Latest Xray observatory snapshot: per-outbound latency, health status and last probe time. Populated only when the Xray config has an observatory configured.

tools.name: get_xray_observatory_history
tools.description: Observatory probe results over time for one outbound tag — the history behind a balancer's current pick.

tag.description: Outbound tag from the observatory config

tools.name: get_xray_template
tools.description: Summarize the saved Xray template — routing rules, balancers, outbounds and DNS — and link to the full JSON at xui://xray/template. The panel merges this template with the auto-generated inbound configs. Pass full=true to get the whole document inline, which is what update_xray_template expects back.

full.description: Return the entire template inline instead of a summary and a link

tools.name: get_xray_versions
tools.description: Get a list of available Xray versions that can be installed.

tools.name: import_clients
tools.description: Create clients from an exported array. Items already present are reported in a 'skipped' list rather than overwritten, so an import cannot clobber a live client.

data.description: The export as a JSON string, e.g. [{"client":{"email":"alice","enable":true},"inboundIds":[7]}]

tools.name: install_xray
tools.description: Install or switch to a specific Xray version.

tools.name: list_api_tokens
tools.description: List the panel's API tokens with their scope, expiry and enabled state. The token values themselves are never returned — the panel stores only hashes.

tools.name: list_client_devices
tools.description: List the HWID devices registered for a client: first and last seen, user agent, OS and model. The hashes themselves are never exposed.

tools.name: list_client_groups
tools.description: List every client group with its member count. Includes empty groups, which exist as placeholders before anyone is added to them.

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: List clients with pagination, search and filtering. Returns a compact page plus totals and a summary.

filter.description: Status filter (e.g. active, depleted, expiring, deactive). Comma-separated for multiple

inbound.description: Filter by inbound id/remark. Comma-separated for multiple

protocol.description: Filter by inbound protocol (e.g. vless, vmess, trojan). Comma-separated for multiple

tools.name: list_clients_paged
tools.description: Filter, sort and page through clients on the server instead of pulling the whole list. Rows are slim — no UUID, password or flow — so this is the tool for finding clients on a large panel; use get_client for the credentials of one.

protocol.description: Only clients attached to an inbound of this protocol

search.description: Case-insensitive match on email, subId or comment

tools.name: list_geodata_categories
tools.description: List the categories inside one geo database, each with its entry count and the attributes its domains carry (e.g. 'ads', 'cn'). These are the codes a routing rule references as geosite:<code> or geoip:<code>.

file.description: Database file name from list_geodata_files, e.g. 'geosite.dat'

limit.description: Rows to return, capped at 500. Omit to return every category — the index is small.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the category code

tools.name: list_geodata_entries
tools.description: List the rules inside one category: domain rules typed as domain/full/keyword/regexp for geosite databases, CIDRs for geoip ones. Use it to check what a category actually matches before routing traffic by it.

limit.description: Rows to return, capped at 500 (the default)

query.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the rule value

tools.name: list_geodata_files
tools.description: List the geo databases (.dat files) in Xray's asset folder, with their detected layout, size, modification time and category count. Start here before writing a routing rule against geosite/geoip categories.

tools.name: list_host_tags
tools.description: List the distinct tags used across all host groups.

tools.name: list_hosts
tools.description: List every host group across all inbounds. A host group publishes one or more inbounds under external addresses — a CDN hostname, a second port, a different SNI — and the panel renders subscription links against them.

tools.name: list_inbounds

instructions:
Control a 3x-ui panel (Xray/V2Ray) over its HTTP API. Tool results are the panel's own JSON.

Conventions that are easy to get wrong:
- Clients are keyed by email, not UUID. add_client attaches a new client to inbound IDs; update_client reads the current record first and overlays only the fields you pass, so anything you omit — the UUID above all — survives.
- update_inbound and update_outbound_sub follow the same read-modify-write contract: pass only what changes. From panel v3.9.0 update_inbound cannot change an inbound's clients or enable flag — use the client tools and set_inbound_enable.
- Routing rules are edited through the whole Xray template, so add/update/remove_routing_rule rewrite it; update_xray_template replaces it outright.
- A balancer override from set_balancer_override lives in the running core only — Xray forgets it on restart.
- "Subscription" means two different things: create/refresh/list_outbound_subs pull remote outbound lists into this panel, while get_subscription_links returns the links this panel serves to its own users.
- Client traffic limits are given in GB in tool parameters; the panel stores bytes.

Every tool is annotated with its effect. Read-only tools are safe to call while exploring; the ones marked destructive delete data, zero counters, or drop live connections.
